free monad and cofree comonad of a container, as containers. NOVELTY DEMOTED 2026-07-14: the COFREE half is prior art in full; the FREE half is an open question in the source that scoops the cofree half.
children.note: TRUST STAYS 'proved' -- the mathematics is correct (trust grades the mathematics, not the novelty). NOVELTY IS DEMOTED TO ZERO ON THE COFREE HALF. Full-PDF audit of Niu-Spivak arXiv:2312.00990 (2026-07-14): the cofree comonad is SCOOPED IN FULL, not merely 'the fact is cited while the container-language derivation and D1-D5 packaging are mine'. Prop. 8.18 (p. 297) gives the carrier t_p := Sigma_{T in tree_p} y^{vtx(T)}. Prop. 8.33 (p. 306) gives THE CATEGORY, item for item: objects = p-trees; a morphism out of T is a rooted path; its codomain is the subtree at the path's end; the identity is the empty path (the root); composition is concatenation. That IS o=root / down=subtree / oplus=concat -- so the D1-D5 packaging claimed as the MacBeth delta is Prop. 8.33. Thm. 8.45 (p. 314): U : Cat# -> Poly has right adjoint T_(-), Poly(c,p) = Cat#(C,T_p), which with Remark 7.18 (polynomial comonoid = comonad) IS the cofree-comonad theorem. (The book credits nobody for any of it, but priority is priority.) Also Prop. 8.57: every T_p is free on a graph. FACTUAL CORRECTION, independent of the novelty question: the directions at T are ALL FINITE ROOTED PATHS, equivalently ALL VERTICES vtx(T) = Sigma_{n in N} p^{lhd n}[pi^{(n)} T] (p. 296) -- NOT leaves and NOT root-to-leaf (maximal) paths, which is how the old note's 'nodes-as-finite-paths' / 'M-tree lhd paths' wording was being read. Maximal paths appear once in the book (Ex. 8.50); an infinite path is a 'ray'. A category whose morphisms out of T were only the maximal paths would have no identities, so the old model was self-refuting. Further: the book never displays a fixed-point equation for tree_p; the closest is Exercise 8.16 (p. 295), 'tree_p is the terminal p-coalgebra', itself uncredited (classically Adamek/Barr) -- so the nu-Y presentation must be attributed to the coalgebra literature, not to this book. WHAT SURVIVES, AND IT IS A PROMOTION: the book NEVER CONSTRUCTS THE FREE MONAD (no free-monad, initial-algebra or W-type section in Ch. 6-9), and characterizing monads in Poly is Chapter 9, Question 11 -- an EXPLICIT OPEN QUESTION. So the free-monad half (C* = (mu Y. 1 + Sigma_s (P(s) -> Y)) lhd (variable-leaf set), monad laws as grafting-monoid laws, and any co-directed D1-D5-style packaging) is NOT prior art and is a live target = Neil's Phase 2. Prior art to clear first: Gambino-Kock arXiv:0906.4931 (free monad on a polynomial is polynomial; positions = P-trees, directions = LEAVES -- for the free monad it genuinely is leaves, which is exactly the distinction the old note collapsed). Caveat on Ch. 9: it cites no one and hedges that its questions 'may or may not be known' -- evidence of the authors' ignorance, not of open-ness in the literature; an independent audit is still owed.

children.approach: THEOREM A: the Day construction (monoidal structures on Set) -> (monoidal structures on Cont) is an EQUIVALENCE onto the 'convolutional' ones, i.e. those whose tensor (D1) preserves coproducts in each variable and (D2) sends representables to representables. Every source in the literature states only the EXISTENCE direction ('for any monoidal structure on Set there IS one on Poly'); no converse, no essential image, no fullness. Mechanism: Cont = Fam(Set^op) is the FREE COPRODUCT COMPLETION of Set^op, so a tensor satisfying (D1) is determined by its restriction to representables, and (D2) says that restriction lands in Set^op.
children.note: CITATIONS ARE PRIORITY ATTRIBUTIONS, NOT PREMISES. Every theorem here is proved from scratch: Prop 2.2 (the Day family is monoidal) is proved directly, not quoted; Prop 5.2 (coherence of Spivak's vee_S) is proved because Spivak only ASSERTS monoidality; Prop 6.2 (invertibility locus of the comparitor) is proved, recovering Spivak eq. (33). So no step rests on 2202.00534, whose extraction level is only agent-summary. 2312.00990 is deep-read (Prop 3.79 quoted verbatim) and is cited for the IDENTIFICATION of the family with Day convolution -- terminology, not a load-bearing lemma. Also: no coend is ever formed, so the size worry about the coend over Set^2 dissolves (Remark 1.4). Lemma 3.2: representability of the unit is a CONSEQUENCE of (D1)+(D2), not an assumption.

children.approach: THEOREM B: for a monoidal (star,I) on Set, the Day tensor is POINTWISE (natural iso p (x) q = p X q, equivalently the extension functor is strong monoidal into ([Set,Set], pointwise product)) iff star = + as bifunctors iff (star,I) = (+,0) monoidally. THEOREM B+: the Day hypothesis is REMOVABLE -- the cartesian structure is the unique pointwise monoidal structure on Cont, among ALL monoidal structures (pointwise forces (D1),(D2), which are invariant under natural iso of the bifunctor, so Theorem A applies). THEOREM B': effective test -- with unit initial, pointwise iff the canonical kappa : A + B -> A star B is a bijection.
children.note: Key sub-lemma 4.4 (RIGIDITY OF THE COPRODUCT): the coproduct on Set admits exactly ONE natural associator and unitors -- they are forced BEFORE coherence is imposed, because Nat(Id_Set, Id_Set) = {id} and a natural map out of a coproduct is its components. Surely folklore but not found stated; it is what makes (star = + as bifunctors) ==> (monoidally iso to (+,0)) go through. Corollary 4.5 retro-explains the dead-end sibling node dirichlet-strict-monoidal. The informal criterion this theorem formalises was already sitting, unproved, in a doc-comment in MacBeth's own Dirichlet.lean -- CHECK OWN LEAN BEFORE CLAIMING. | VERIFIED: kappa is an iso iff S = empty (Thm 5.4). SHARPENING recorded: for a FIXED pair (A,B) with A or B empty, kappa_{A,B} is bijective for EVERY S (the middle piece A x S x B vanishes trivially). Correct statements: kappa_{A,B} bijective iff |A|.|S|.|B| = 0; kappa bijective for ALL A,B iff S = empty. Both Thm B' and Thm 5.4 quantify over all A,B, so both are correct as stated. kappa is ALWAYS injective -- it is the inclusion of the two outer summands, and its image always misses exactly the middle piece. That middle piece IS the obstruction.

children.approach: Spivak's family A vee_S B := A + A x S x B + B (Reference eq. 9, credited to R. Consequence (Cor 5.5): Cont carries a PROPER CLASS of pairwise non-isomorphic convolutional monoidal structures ALL SHARING THE TERMINAL OBJECT AS UNIT, exactly one of which (S=0) is the cartesian product.
children.note: Spivak ASSERTS monoidality without proof (Reference eq. 9); Niu-Spivak Ex. 3.82 asks the reader to check associativity for S=1 only. The coherence proof is supplied here because Cor. 5.5 needs it. The punchline is that this family DEFEATS EVERY CHEAP INVARIANT: same unit as the product, symmetric, convolutional -- only kappa (Theorem B') separates them. This answers the PROVE.md worry 'is the Day family actually large?' with a proper class. | VERIFIED 2026-07-14 (scratch/day-family/): pentagon and triangle checked ELEMENTWISE (243 size-tuples, |A|,|B|,|C|,|D|,|S| in {0,1,2}, plus size-3 spot checks; the two composites are equal AS FUNCTIONS, not merely equinumerous). The coherence proof fills a real gap in the cited sources. | SYMMETRY DELIBERATELY NOT CLAIMED: there is an evident candidate braiding and Spivak states his (.) construction for SYMMETRIC monoidal structures on Set, but MacBeth never checked the hexagon. A braiding must re-match the S-separators, and the negative control shows separator-rematching is EXACTLY where coherence fails. Nothing needs symmetry (Cor 5.5 needs only monoidal + pairwise non-isomorphic), so the claim was dropped rather than assumed. Open if anyone wants it.

children.approach: THEOREM C: the comparitor o_{p,q} : p (x) q -> p <| q is the COUNIT OF A CORFLECTION. Precisely, p (x) - = Lan_J((p <| -) . J) along the representable embedding J : Set^op -> Cont; i.e. p (x) - is the free coproduct-preserving functor agreeing with p <| - on representables, and for every coproduct-preserving F, postcomposition with the comparitor is a bijection Nat(F, p (x) -) = Nat(F, p <| -). So p (x) - is the TERMINAL coproduct-preserving approximation to p <| -. Reason it exists: <| satisfies (D2) exactly and (D1) only in the LEFT variable, and its restriction to representables is (A,B) -> A x B -- the SAME restriction as the Dirichlet tensor. So (x) is the Day-ification of <|, and the comparitor is the universal map.
children.note: THE MAP ITSELF IS PRIOR ART (see sibling dirichlet-is-uniform-fragment-of-seq for the six citations). What is new is the UNIVERSAL PROPERTY: in the literature the comparitor is always DERIVED by plugging y into the duoidal interchanger (p<|p')(x)(q<|q') -> (p(x)q)<|(p'(x)q'). Theorem C says what it IS, and two known facts become corollaries: it exists (it is a counit), and it is invertible when q is representable (the counit of Lan_J is invertible on the image of a fully faithful J). Prop 6.1.1 verifies the associator coherence BY HAND rather than appealing to an unchecked monoidal-Kan principle -- note Niu-Spivak Ex. 6.85 and Spivak eq. (32) state the lax monoidality with OPPOSITE source/target; only Spivak's direction type-checks. Prop 6.2 sharpens Spivak eq. (33) to an EXACT trichotomy (iso iff q representable, or q=0 with every p[s] nonempty, or |S_q|>=2 and p linear). Prop 6.3: the comparitor is NOT INJECTIVE either (p=1=y^0 collapses all shapes of q) -- MacBeth's earlier note recorded only non-surjectivity. Non-surjectivity measures where <| is DEPENDENT; non-injectivity measures where <| is VACUOUS. That is why (x) is a coreflection of <| and not a subobject of it. | VERIFIED: iso-criterion exhaustive over all C,D with <=2 shapes and <=2 positions/shape, no counterexample; non-injectivity and non-surjectivity witnesses explicit; C (x) y^B = C <| y^B on 244 pairs. NOTE the verification run's own summary mis-stated the criterion as '|p[s]|=1 or |S_q|<=1'; that is WRONG for S_q = empty with p[s] = empty (c_s : empty -> empty^empty = 1 is not surjective). Prop 6.2's trichotomy is correct and cross-checks against Lemma 2.4: 1 (x) 0 = 0 but 1 <| 0 = 1. Sub-agent summaries are 'computed' at best -- re-derive before trusting.

CLAIM (2026-07-14, MacBeth): a Day-convolutional structure (x)_star on Cont is CLOSED iff the corepresentable Set(R,-) preserves star; with the narrative of a 'pointwise/closed duality' (x is pointwise but hard to close; (x)_Dir is not pointwise but easy to close).
children.reason: REFUTED 2026-07-14, same day it was made. COUNTEREXAMPLE to the ==> direction: the categorical product x on Cont IS the Day convolution of (Set,+,0) (Niu-Spivak 2312.00990 Prop 3.79; registry sibling day-family-classification). The corepresentable Set(R,-) does NOT preserve + (for |R| >= 2, Set(R,A+B) is not Set(R,A) + Set(R,B)). So a structure whose corepresentable fails to preserve star is nevertheless closed: the criterion is FALSE. The 'pointwise/closed duality' narrative dies with it -- there is no duality, x is BOTH pointwise AND closed. Refuted by argument against an established theorem (refutation: proved), not by taste. WHAT SURVIVES, and must not be over-pruned: the POINTWISE criterion 'does the corepresentable SPLIT the domain tensor (y^(A+B) = y^A x y^B, y^(AxB) does not split)' is a DIFFERENT claim, it is about pointwiseness, not closedness, and it stands (see sibling pointwise-uniqueness). children.approach: THE SALVAGE (new, modest, believed true). UNIFORM CLOSURE FORMULA: for a Day-convolutional (x)_star on Cont, the internal hom is [p,q]_star = Prod_{I : p(1)} q <| (p[I] star y), i.e. [p,q]_star(A) = Prod_{I} q(A star p[I]). One-line proof: Poly(r (x)_star p, q) = Prod_{J,I} q(r[J] star p[I]) = Poly(r, [p,q]_star). EXISTENCE CONDITION (corrected today): R star (-) must be a POLYNOMIAL functor (preserve wide pullbacks) for every set R -- NOT, as first claimed, that star be closed on Set. Substituting star = + gives the cartesian closure (Niu-Spivak Thm 5.31), star = x gives the Dirichlet closure (Eq. 4.79), star = vee_S gives Spivak's third family. Spivak's Eqs. (38)/(39)/(40) are exactly these three instances written SIDE BY SIDE -- the general theorem is never stated in the book. That gap is the claim.

children.approach: CONJECTURE (comparitor no-go). Id : (Cont,lhd,y) -> (Cont,otimes,y) is LAX monoidal with structure map the comparitor o_{p,q} : p otimes q -> p lhd q (its coherence IS the duoidal interchange, Spivak 2202.00534 Eq. 29 -- CHECK, do not assume). Lax transports MONOIDS, not comonoids. Hence: every container monad (a lhd-monoid) is a Dirichlet monoid, via A otimes A --o--> A lhd A --mu--> A. But a directed container (a lhd-comonoid, registry m3-comonoid-forward) does NOT descend to a Dirichlet comonoid: that needs A lhd A -> A otimes A, the comparitor REVERSED, which is not invertible (non-surjectivity machine-checked, see dirichlet-is-uniform-fragment-of-seq). Predicted boundary, from Spivak Eq. 33 (Indep iso when p linear or q representable) on the diagonal p=q=C: transfer survives IFF C is degenerate -- C = y^A (one shape; the directed container is a monoid on A) or C = Ay (one position per shape; a discrete category). GENERAL LESSON: an approximation is a one-way street -- it builds maps OUT of a tensor, never INTO one; variance of the structure map decides which structures survive Day-ification.

KILL LINE: Shapiro-Spivak arXiv:2305.00167 Remark 3.16 -- 'Poly_E is a full subcategory of the category of dependent lenses [Spivak 1908.02202 Ex 3.5] whose objects are ALL morphisms in E; allowing such objects does not interfere with the CATEGORY, only the MONOIDAL STRUCTURE required the objects to be exponentiable.' That IS 'the equivalence needs only pullbacks; only <| needs Pi.' Plus SS23 Thm 5.6 (comonoids in Poly_E = internal categories with exponentiable source, any finite-limit E), Cor 5.12 (morphisms = internal cofunctors, adopting Clarke Def 12), Example 5.10 (exponentiable-source is a PROPER restriction: not every double category is Conduche). What is MacBeth's, and is ONLY expository (not registry-worthy as a theorem): (i) the 5+2=7 law accounting -- two internal-category axioms absorbed into the dependent typing of o and oplus -- and the reading of every dependent cast as a pullback-mediation obligation discharged by an earlier law (D1 enables the left-unit mediating map; D2 enables the associativity source map); (ii) the correction Cat(B) -> Cat_D(B) (source = display map; = Cat(B) iff q = cod_B); (iii) a fresh witness that the <|-packaging is strictly lossy off LCC -- (Q,+) as a one-object topological category in Top has non-exponentiable source (Q not core-compact; Day-Kelly), an instance of SS23 Example 5.10's phenomenon in a new base -- and the tidy iff: Cat(E) = Comon(Poly_E) iff E is LCC.
